title: EVA: An Efficient and Versatile Generative Engine for Targeted Discovery of Novel Analog Circuits
problem: Discovering entirely new, high-performance analog circuit topologies is an underexplored challenge; current AI methods focus on topology synthesis from known structures rather than generative discovery of novel designs.
motivation: Advanced applications (AI, 5G/6G, quantum computing) demand novel analog circuit topologies, but manual expertise-driven discovery is slow; generative AI methods can accelerate topology discovery if trained to generate valid, diverse, high-performing circuits.
method: EVA builds novel circuits by using an AI model called a decoder-only transformer that predicts where electronic components should connect, one connection at a time, starting from scratch. First, the model learns general patterns by studying thousands of existing circuit designs (pretraining). Then it's optimized using PPO and DPO—techniques that reward high-performing designs—to generate circuits tailored for specific performance goals.
key_novelty: Discovers entirely new circuit designs from scratch by sequentially predicting how to connect electronic components, using a decoder-only transformer optimized with PPO and DPO.
contributions: Pretraining strategy on unlabeled circuit topologies building foundational connectivity knowledge
Two fine-tuning methods (PPO, DPO) enabling targeted discovery of high-performing topologies
Demonstrated validity, novelty, versatility, and sample efficiency across multiple circuit types
limitations: Specific performance metrics (power, area, frequency) and comparison to other generative methods not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Generative transformer for novel analog circuit discovery
